title: Rediscovering Kingdom Prayer
paragraphs: Our focus tonight is first on prayer, and afterwards we will talk about fasting. I would like to start by talking a little about the concept of the Kingdom of God and why we should pray. We all know that God's original purpose for man was to rule over the earth on His behalf. We also know that man was created to rule over the earth and its resources as a representative of God. The Bible is clear about that. When man disobeyed God, he fell.

The Fall of Man was therefore not the Fall from heaven, but the Fall of Dominion. That means governance over the earth. Man was created to lead in an area of giftedness on earth, and man was created to fulfill God's purpose on earth by using that gift to control the resources on earth and to give glory to God. That is why God created us all, 7 billion of us on this earth. God still had that plan for us. That leads to my final point and introduction. Vision is a glimpse of your prayer.

When you see what you were born for, it is truly what you are meant to do to represent God. Vision should be a point of prayer. When you pray, you ought to pray from the substance of your vision. In other words, you do not ask God for something that *you* want done. You ask God to do something that He has commanded you to do. That is what prayer is. It is the other way around. We normally pray to ask God for something that we want. But true, sincere prayer is actually giving God permission to do what He wants.

And then instruct Him to do it through your authority on earth, which we will talk about in a moment. In Matthew chapter 6, Jesus spoke about people who worry about things, and this is again related to prayer. He says: "Why do you worry about what you will eat? The birds do not worry as much as you do. Why do you worry about what you will drink? Birds do not worry about that. The animals are taken care of." And then He says: "Are you not much more valuable than these animals?

If God takes care of them, He will also take care of you. So prayer is not a matter of praying for food, clothing, houses, and cars. He says: 'Don't even worry about that.'" "" So, of course he cancels our prayer list. "And then we must not forget that your self-worth is therefore determined by your priorities. What you think is important, that is what you will focus on. Perhaps this is the reason why our prayers are often not answered.

Jesus is now teaching us, in this whole process, that there are keys by which we must live in the kingdom of God and according to which we must function. I want to talk briefly about keys. Please write this down. Keys are the principles, the laws, or the regulations that influence change and operation. That is what keys are. The Bible speaks of the keys of the kingdom. It is actually about the laws, the regulations, and the principles by which the kingdom functions. That is why keys stand for certain things.

First, they stand for authority. They also stand for access, ownership, or control. Keys stand for authorization. Keys also stand for power. They stand for freedom and, above all, they stand for permission. If I give you the keys to my house, you have that whole list, don't you? Look at that list. If I give you the keys to my house, you have everything that is on that list. Have Am I right? You have the authority to enter my house. You have a sense of ownership. You can take over my house.

A key also gives you control over my house. It gives you authorization to go in and out whenever you want. It also gives you the power to control my house, to enter my house or to come out. It gives you power. Keys also give you the freedom to move in and out of my house and to act. And that freedom gives you permission. Because I gave you my keys. So when the Bible says that God gave us keys, it means that God gave us all this authority, access, power, and permission.

He says: "I will give you the keys, not of the kingdom of heaven, but of the kingdom of heaven." Which means that you have the authority, access, power, and permission to function in the kingdom of God on earth. "In fact, the next verse in that chapter, if you read it, He says: " So what you bind on earth—binding means locking up—" will be locked up in heaven. "What you open or allow on earth will be allowed in heaven.

In other words, heaven will do exactly what the earth says it must do, because the earth holds the keys to heaven. Prayer is one of those keys. And I am going to talk about it. In fact, prayer is the most important key, but it is the most misunderstood key, because it is the key that unlocks all other keys. I will explain that in a moment. When you understand prayer, you will never stop praying. People do not pray because they do not understand prayer. I am always praying. I pray all the time.

I know that sounds rather, you know, rather spiritual, but no. Prayer is a conscious awareness that you must constantly grant access to the earth, uh, heaven. That awareness ensures that I pray all the time. Again, I must correct your concept of prayer, because when I use the word prayer, you get the wrong image in your head. So sometimes you think that if he prays, that means that he also, you know, that he is driving and kneeling in his car." while he is driving.

Look, because your concept is so distorted by your religious culture that even the idea of ​​the word prayer conjures up a certain image in your mind of someone kneeling with hands folded and, you know, saying religious things. No. We are going to discuss exactly why that is not prayer. The problem with prayer is that everyone prays.

Muslims pray, Buddhists pray, scientists pray, Scientologists prefer to pray, Bahá'is pray, you know, Rastafarians pray, Buddhists pray, Christians pray, animists pray, witches pray; everyone prays to someone. So prayer is not unique to any one of us. It depends on what you mean by prayer. However, prayer is not an option for the believer. Prayer is not an option for us. Please write that down. I think we have n't understood this yet. I am so proud of you. I am proud of you because you are here.

I think it is wonderful to see people enthusiastic about praying and fasting. I think God is the most enthusiastic God tonight. Of all his At times I think that this is also the most exciting part. He says: " If my people, if my people would only come now and seek me." We put ourselves in the position to seek God. God is waiting for that. Prayer is not an option for us. It is a necessity. Prayer is the most common experience of every believer.

Everyone prays, but the problem is that prayer is the most talked-about experience, yet the least experienced in terms of results. All Christians pray, but most do not attend prayer meetings. In fact, the smallest gathering in any church is the prayer service. If you study all the churches in your country, especially the Christian ones, people do not attend prayer meetings. Usually, they pass prayer meetings on to elderly people who have nothing else to do.

You know, they say: "Well, since you are retired, you might as well become an intercessor." I am afraid I have to disappoint you: intercession as a specific ministry does not exist in the Bible. If I say that, let me phrase it this way. The gift of intercession is not a gift in the Bible. There is no ministry of prayer in the Bible. I have read the Bible a few times, believe me. I have checked it. There is no ministry of prayer in the Bible.

In other words, you cannot say: those seven elderly people, they were called to pray. That is not in the Bible. No one is called to pray. Not a single group of people. But we have created that ministry for God. Do you know why? So that we can stay home and watch the NBA while the elderly pray on Monday night. Or we can go to a club while they pray. We can go to a meeting while they pray. We can watch TV while they pray. Why? Because we don't want to pray. Why? Because we don't see results.

That is why we don't pray. And we want others to pray for us so that we don't have to pray. What a tragedy. And that is why the prayer service is the least attended gathering in almost 100% of the churches worldwide. Now, why? And that is because we don't see results. I think I always give an example. Have you ever gone to a soda vending machine, put your money in, and no drink came out? What did you do after that? No, you tried again, right? Put money in one more time. You tried it. And what happened?

Nothing came out. What do you do the third time? Well, you kick it. You say: "Wow!" "What else do you do? You shake it. What else do you do? You keep an eye on whether no one is listening. You say a few words to the machine. You say: 'Father, forgive me for what I said.'" "Okay? Yes. And what do you do when you're done with that? What do you do then? You walk away. Very important. You walk away from the vending machine. Are you tempted to go back to that vending machine? No, you actually avoid it. Why?

No result achieved. When a person gets no result from something, he stops doing it. This, this is the problem with prayer. You pray and you pray and you pray and you pray, and you pray, and you get no result, so treat your prayer like that vending machine you didn't get a drink from. You say that this doesn't work, and so you stay away from it. And this is a normal human reaction to disappointment. So the question then is: is there something wrong with prayer? Is there something wrong with you?

Or is there something wrong with praying? Look, we need to figure out what is going on here. If God says that He answers prayers and you don't get what He promised, then there must be something in the system that you are not executing correctly. And the question is: is there something wrong with prayer, something wrong with God, something wrong with Is it you, or is there something wrong with the praying? Well, I had the same problem. I did n't like praying myself because I did n't get any results.

I had the same problem that people go through. I even went to those prayer meetings that lasted all night. Tried to stay awake all night. I keep wondering why they bring pillows to a prayer meeting that lasts all night. But people do that. That is, I grew up in the Baptist church. They brought pillows too, just in case. And usually that was the case. And they called it persevering all night. We were supposed to persevere. And what was amazing is that we persevered and prayed, and nothing happened.

The only thing we did was get tired and sleepy at the end of it. Because no matter how hard you do something, if you do it the wrong way, you are only doing it hard the wrong way. So the point is not how hard you pray, how long you pray, how refined your words are, you know, how serious you are. That doesn't matter. If you don't understand it and it If you do not execute it correctly and do not have the right approach, the results are the same. You will have an automaton that you will kick.

This is why we need to talk about prayer. Now, a few things about prayer that are important. One, without God, man cannot do it. But without man, God will not do it. These words were spoken by John Wesley, the founder of Methodism, a very powerful man. He was known for his prayer life. A very powerful gentleman. And he wrote this down. He finally understood what I had already discovered years ago as a teenager. What he is actually trying to say is that God can do nothing on earth without a human being involved.

But he also means that man gets nothing done on earth without the involvement of God. Therefore, there must be a collaboration between divinity and humanity to get things done on earth. That is what he means. It is a very important principle. It is very true. In any case, write down point two. What happens on earth therefore depends on you. When I discovered that, everything in my life changed. Us is the opposite. learned. What happens on earth depends on God, we say. So we have been taught to be dependent on God.

Trust in God. Just let God do it. The Bible actually teaches something else. It teaches that God is actually dependent on you to do things on earth. That leads to principle number three. Prayer is therefore, in my humble view, defined as giving an earthly license to heaven to intervene. Prayer is man giving heaven an earthly license to intervene on earth. Prayer is man giving heaven permission to intervene in the affairs of the earth.

Prayer is humanity giving heaven access to the earth through the authority man has received from God. That is prayer. This is why prayer is necessary. Do you get it now? It is necessary because God can do nothing on earth without the cooperation of a human being. You know, when I teach this, people go crazy. I mean, the internet sometimes asks: "What is he talking about?" God is sovereign. God is almighty. He can do anything.

Well, if God can do everything, why doesn't he stop the wars, the crime, the murders, the rapes, and that last divorce of yours? Why does n't God solve all poverty on earth? Do you think God is happy to see people starving, begging, and selling their bodies on the street? If he can do everything, can you tell me that a loving God who made people sits back and watches while he can solve it? If that is true, I do not want to serve that God.

Who wants to serve a God who watches as babies are aborted in hospitals, dumped in buckets with their heads cut off, and does not intervene supernaturally? What kind of God watches as people break into others' homes, steal their flat-screen TVs, load their furniture into a car, and drive away with people's hard-earned money? Come on, what kind of God looks at that while he can solve it? Do not jump to conclusions about certain matters. I am convinced that John Wesley realized this.

Man cannot do without God, but without man, God does not want to intervene. If you read the Scriptures carefully, these are principles that are fully supported by Scripture. And I will read a few to you during this process. So let's talk about why we need dedication. I told you that God is more enthusiastic about devotion than you are. That is because God says: "Finally, I have a few days during which people have turned to me to give me permission to set things right on earth." God is enthusiastic.

This is why the devil does not want you to fast and pray. He will work against you until day eight. And then he will leave you alone. I promise you that all your friends will ask you out for lunch over the next 7 days. And they even promise to pay. In fact, all invitations for elaborate meals are arriving exactly this month. That is just how the devil thinks. If only I can make you break, for you are about to disrupt my plan on earth. Tell the devil that it is too late.

Yes, so as soon as we dedicate ourselves to this fasting, hell is in trouble and heaven is thrilled. May I hear an amen throughout the whole world? Praise the Lord. And that is why I am so enthusiastic. We have hundreds of people here, and even more are coming tomorrow. And people are going to open themselves up and say to God: "Come through me." That is what makes me enthusiastic about prayer and fasting. Look at Luke chapter 6. I want to talk about the value of prayer, its importance. And this is just an example.

Jesus Christ, it says that one day he went to a hillside to pray. And how long did he stay there? Praying to God all night long. This is interesting. Jesus Christ is God. But he took on a human form for 33 years to accomplish the work we call redemption. He knew that upon his arrival on earth he would assume a human form, a human body. That means that he had to give his father permission to intervene through him. So it was his daily practice. But this time he prayed all night. What would he do praying all night?

What would he say? Interesting question. Mark 6:45. Once again, I want you to see how important prayer is, even for Jesus. Matthew chapter 6 verse 45: "After He had left them, He went up the mountain again to pray." He said, it simply records how important this habit was to Him, this what He did. Now pay attention, I want you to notice something. No, I'm going to let you figure it out afterwards. Let me see if I can see how smart you are. Luke 22 verse 46 reads: "Why are you sleeping?" He asked.

"Stand up and pray, so that you do not fall into temptation." What strikes you about these moments when Jesus prayed? What do you notice? Can you tell me? Will someone shout it out loud? He prayed alone. Write that down. You see, He had no group prayer life. He had a personal prayer life. Most of you are waiting for January because you have no prayer life in February. No prayer life in April. You have no prayer life in September. You, you need the team spirit. But I discovered something.

If you do not develop a personal prayer life, you will not enjoy a communal prayer life. Jesus prayed alone. One day, I tried to find in the four Gospels of the New Testament where Jesus prayed with his disciples. Guess what? I could n't find it. That shocked me. Well, maybe He did, but there is no record that He did. Every time He was referred to in prayer, it was that He went alone. Which means that you must develop a personal prayer life with God, which is your private time with God, always.

Stop waiting for other people to give you access to God. He understood it. And He said to them: you must pray so that you do not come into temptation. If you keep giving God access, you can never go wrong. You can never do anything wrong. If you keep giving God access. Is that clear? I talk about the relationship of the kingdom, the kingdom of God, and prayer. A kingdom is a country with a government. We know that. And governments function on what we call laws, constitutional laws.

And laws are made to guarantee the promises in the constitution. So, a prayer is what we call a legal request. This is very important. The word prayer in the original Hebrew is actually the word request. Request. Request is not a religious word. So, in the Bible we have, uh, prayer is not a religious activity at all. It is a legal activity. It means submitting a request. Uh, a request is actually only possible where there is a government, a constitution, and citizens.

Because a petition is the legal demand that the citizen makes of the government based on the rights and privileges that the constitution and the laws grant to citizens. Prayer is therefore a legal activity. What did I say? Prayer is a legal activity. I know this is difficult to understand. You know, we... we... when we talk about prayer, we usually get into this religious mood, you know, O Lord. If you tried that in a courtroom, they would throw you out. Prayer is a petition.

A petition means demanding an authority based on rights. So when the Bible says 'pray', it is actually telling you: demand from me what I have legally promised. Therefore, prayer must be taught. Do you know why you hire a lawyer? Because you do not know your own rights. And the lawyer ought to have studied the law and the constitution. And you pay him to tell you your rights and show you how you can exercise them. In other words, the lawyer files a petition on your behalf. Right, the word petition one more time.

Do you also know what the word petition means? It means pleading. Plead, p-l-e-i-t-e-n. Lawyers in this room will tell you that that is what they do. The work of a lawyer is to plead your case. Pleading a case means that the lawyer gathers all the necessary information to prove that the rights you claim are legally yours. That is the word prayer. This is why you don't have to make up your own words when praying. Oh, man. You know, and that is also a reason why people don't pray, because they have no words left.

They say: "Well, you know, how can you pray for an hour? After ten minutes I have nothing left to say." That's why people don't pray, because we have the whole wrong concept that you have to make up all those sentences and try to impress God, you know? And we even use words that God does not understand, such as you mighty almighty holy holy, which God said: "Listen, just present your case." And we try to impress God more than we try to reach God.

All the material you need to plead your case before God is in the Bible. In fact, you cannot claim anything that is not in the Bible. So you should add nothing to your prayer except what is in the Bible. The Bible provides you with the material for everything you need to plead your case. You know, lawyers are interesting. We have one here. He will tell you that lawyers really aren't smart people, you know.

They just have a good memory, or what they ca n't remember, listen, what they ca n't remember is in the cupboard. We pay them to find out which book it is in. That is all. Sorry lawyers, but you know it is true. Don't try to impress me. A lawyer is someone who sat in a lecture hall somewhere for two years to learn where things stand. And they are learning the constitution. That's it. And we pay them to find the information. They do not make up any information themselves. It 's already here.

They're just lining it up for you. When you come before God to tempt God, you must first do your research. So you go to the library. As a lawyer, you have your own library. It is called the Bible. There are 66 books on a shelf. And each book contains a whole lot of constitutional promises and privileges and commitments that the government has made. And you must go there, take the material, and say: "Lord, do this."

But we are so religiously possessed by spirits that God is not sure of, that we come before God, throw a scarf over our heads, act very profound, you know, and then: oh, yes, Lord. I am going to pray now, Lord. And we do all that gymnastics and emotional, you know, and God says, "What are you doing?" Jesus once said to the Pharisees: " You think that you will be heard because of your many words." Prayer is making a request. Submitting a request is simply demanding what is already yours, promised by your government.

Am I being clear now? You are supposed to have fun for the next 21 days. You are supposed to take the Constitution and find a matter or promise somewhere in the Constitution. Both. A matter or a promise. And then you say: "Okay, God, based on what I really need on earth right now, I am going to look up this matter in section so-and-so, subsection three, article 45." And this is the matter. I am now going to request your attention regarding this matter for the next 20 minutes.

And when I am finished, I know that you heard me. Yes. Why? Because I do not pray my will, I pray Your will. And if I know that you have heard me, then I know that I have it. It says: "The request that I asked of you." So, what do I do next? I walk out of the courtroom, the embassy, ​​the diplomatic center, and I thank Him all the way home that it is already accomplished. Praise God. Why? For the Bible says in 1 John: "If we know that He hears us, we pray according to His will." Not yours.

Do not bring your will to God. His will is written. That is called the Word of God. Now, what is prayer? Let's define it then. Prayer is, please write this down. I'll give you time to write this down. Take a picture of it. Use your camera, take a picture of it, and give me the credits. Prayer is the legal claim for promises and rights submitted to the government by a citizen of good standing based on constitutional laws. Very important definition. Prayer is, let's say it out loud.

Prayer is the legal claim for promises and rights submitted to the government by a citizen of good standing based on constitutional law. That is prayer. Practical definition. That is why it is called a petition. Now pay attention to the words 'good reputation'. Don't forget that. You know, uh, if you go to the city center, uh, to the courthouse, the Supreme Court, and you demand from the judges that you receive your constitutional rights, but you are wanted for a robbery. The judge can say: " First, arrest him."

"Because you currently have no right whatsoever to appear before us." You have broken the laws of the land. Many people come before God and they are not qualified to make demands. And of course, we now have the teaching going around where they say: "No, you don't need to be qualified, because Jesus is qualified for you." I have a problem with that. Because you tell me that I can still live in any way whatsoever and still appear before God and get things done. There is something wrong with this concept.

Let me quote one of God's concepts. If I harbor injustice in my heart, the Lord will not even hear my case. What about this one? Direct from Jesus. When you come and present your petition to the Lord, if the Holy Spirit reminds you that you have something against someone, do not offer your petition. Go and set it right first, He says, then come back and the Lord will forgive your sin and He will hear you. You don't just walk into God's courtroom as if you are qualified after breaking the law.

Every lawyer will tell you, you know, if you break the law, you come under judgment, not under rights. Judgement. Therefore, prayer requires that the supplicant has a good status. Are you still following me? And that is why I am so enthusiastic tonight, because when you fast and add fasting to prayer, your position to demand things from your government becomes 20 times stronger. That is why the demons could not come out of that little boy when the disciples prayed.

They were holy men, they loved Jesus, they were obedient to God, but they had too much pizza in their stomachs. Sorry. And the Bible says that they prayed against that demon and he did not come out. For the demon knew that what is needed to get me out requires less food. That is what Jesus said to them. He said: "This demon could not be cast out because this kind," he says, "does not go out except by prayer and fasting." There needs to be a little more sacrifice on your part to get some things done mentally.

I am excited that God will bless you during this fast. Is anyone ready for extra things to be done? Why do n't we thank Him already that something powerful is about to happen? Hallelujah. I mean, God will break through to you. Praise the Lord. Some things you have tried to get done will require this fasting. Not only prayer. What is prayer? Another definition. Prayer is demanding of the government that it carries out what it has promised to the citizen. And they do that because you have a right.

This entire year is actually a year of justice and rights. And God wants you to learn this first. Therefore, this is a good starting point for this year to talk about your rights as a citizen. I am currently finishing my book on citizenship. Hopefully it comes out later this year, I hope so. But in that book, I do a lot of research and explore many of your rights as a citizen of the Kingdom. If you know your rights, you will become dangerous in heaven. And also in hell.

For if you know your rights, you beg no longer. You demand. Can I hear ' demands'? Can I hear an amen? To demand. Thirdly, prayer is submitting the constitutional promises to the government. No complications. Prayer is what? Submitting the constitutional promises to the government. That makes prayer simple. Now, that is why you should read the book. You don't read the Bible to be spiritual. You don't read the Bible so that people can say you are a Christian or something like that.

You read the Bible because you want to know your rights, your privileges, and your promises from your own government. So, when you file your petition, you do so on the basis of what has been promised by law. You are holding the government's own constitution up to it. Listen to the words of God, who is the ultimate government. He says: "Bring my word to me, for I guard my word to carry it out. For behold, I want to do what I have said, but bring it back to me so that I may have permission to do it." Let us pray.

Prayer is taking the word of God and saying: "God, this is what You have promised. Now I demand that You do it, because I stand in a position of authority as a human being on earth." Praying is easy if you understand it. Praying is not begging. Praying is demanding. Uh, let me give you some examples, okay? Uh, how often should you pray? And why is praying so important that you must always do it? In Luke 18:1, that is verse 1, chapter 18.

It says: "And he spoke a parable to them, to teach them that people should always what? Pray and not slacken. " Remember, every time you see the word pray, stop thinking religiously. He says: "People always have to do something? Make a request. They always have to make demands based on what God has promised them. They should always make demands. All day long, wherever you are, which means that you really have to know the word of God, remember it, keep it in your mind, and read it.

And by the way, uh, you might not be able to know the whole book literally by heart, but you do have to read the whole book. Because the Bible says that the Holy Spirit, who is your counselor—what is a counselor? A lawyer—will remind you of the things you have learned. You know, uh, the lawyers here will tell you that they don't just memorize the cases you are talking about. But they go to their library and they leaf through all the books to see which one they read it in again. They act like the Holy Spirit.

That is why they are called counselors. Lawyers are called counselors. They go looking and they say: 'Okay, you have a specific case, I need to go to section B of the library.'" I have to go to aisle 16. I have to go to volume 175. " Then I have to go to the subsection in the book, you know, section 60, then I go to article 52, and then I find the case in 1864." And they find him. "And it says:" And Daniel was not afraid of the lion. Then they come back and say: "Look, uh, right now they are threatening your jobs."

They can take your job away from you. But according to that case from the past, the government took care of Daniel. Government, we can present this to the government for you and tell the government that they must take care of you too. So you are using a case to submit a request on behalf of another citizen. You read the Bible. I love the Bible. You know, God is so amazing. Whenever people became afraid, God said: "Do you remember what I did to Egypt?" He cited a case. You don't get it. You don't understand.

If you are broke, remember that the Israelites were also broke. So cite a case: "Lord, You made the Egyptians favorably disposed toward the Israelites and they gave them much money." Today, my rent must be paid. Now, do n't sit there crying: "Oh God, I do n't know where the money is going to come from." That is not a prayer. You get the case. You say: "Lord, I am more qualified than the Israelites, for they were not under the blood of Jesus Christ." They stood covered in the blood of a lamb.

And today, as a citizen, I demand that you not... do not embarrass yourself. You must handle this case just as you handled their case. Grant me favor regarding my rent. "If you want to hear God speak to me, then get your rent paid. He will speak to me. Bring me all the way to your house. But what are you doing? You are sitting there crying. God said: 'Do not cry.'" "" Submit a request. "That is prayer. If you cry in a courtroom, the judge stops the case. Don't believe me? Go to the center and try it.

When you start crying, the judge always stops the case. He says: ' We are taking a 15-minute break.'" "" Go pull yourself together. "He says. Why? Because emotions do n't win cases in a courtroom. I mean, cases can influence emotions. You get excited, you know, because you 've won the case. But it wasn't the emotions that won the case. Just make a note of this. Jesus said: "There was a judge in a city." "Now, look at verse one. He spoke a parable about what? Prayer. Now, verse two." There was a city with a judge.

"Look, He didn't say there was a priest in a robe. Come on, you'll understand. He's talking about prayer. He went straight to a legal courtroom. That is why our prayers are not answered. We come in a robe. With, you know, rosaries and beads and candles, and God says: 'No, bring me a law book and a lawyer.'" " What is He talking about? Prayer. Do you get it yet? Look at him. He says that this judge was so mean. He did not fear God and did not like people. Sounds like some people we know, doesn't it?

This man was in a difficult position. He had the power, but did not love people and did not respect humanity. He wanted nothing to do with people and nothing to do with God. He did not believe in God. He chose the worst judge, you know, to prove his case. Next verse, verse three. And who was there? A single woman without a husband, broke and on welfare. He chooses the poorest, most helpless person in their culture of that time: a widow. A widow was the lowest social status in the time of Jesus. Let me tell you why.

Because if a woman married a man in the time of Jesus, and he had brothers, if her husband died, the next brother would take her into his home as his wife. Not necessarily to love her, but to protect the family name. So he was obliged to let her live with him and he had to provide for her for the rest of her life." caring on behalf of his brother, to protect his brother's name, which is the family name.
